newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates ends up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates ends up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed up across the board on Monday due to a number of new domestic A share issues this week and a sharp rise on the A share markets today, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract surged to 15.88 percent from 10.52 percent last Friday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market rose to 10.48 million lots from 7.1 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.

Three new A share firms will issue stocks this week on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges and traders said this made big institutions borrow money on the repo market on Monday to prepare for bidding for the stocks.
The solid gains in the A share indices on both exchanges on Monday also promoted borrowing on the repo market, they said.
Traders said the repo rates would stay at high levels in the next few days due to the new share issues and expected strong performance on the A share markets.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended down across the board on Monday.
Traders said the active and strong A share markets sucked much liquidity out of the spot market, pushing down the prices.
The most active three-year bond that matured in 1999 fell to 104.90 yuan from 105.13 yuan.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market rose to 1.07 million lots from 917,668 lots.
Despite the day's fall, traders said they believed sentiment and fundamentals for the spot market were good and that the prices were likely to recover shortly.
